title: How to Reset Your CloudDash Password
content:
CloudDash provides two methods for resetting your password depending on how your account was created: email/password login, or SSO (Single Sign-On) via your identity provider.

## Method 1: Standard Email/Password Reset

If you log in with an email address and password:

1. Navigate to https://app.clouddash.io/login
2. Click **Forgot Password** below the login form.
3. Enter the email address associated with your CloudDash account.
4. Click **Send Reset Link**. A password reset email will arrive within 2 minutes.
5. Open the email and click **Reset My Password**. This link is valid for 60 minutes.
6. Enter your new password. Requirements: minimum 12 characters, at least one uppercase letter, one number, and one special character.
7. Click **Set New Password**. You will be redirected to the login page.

**Did not receive the email?** Check your spam or junk folder. Add noreply@clouddash.io to your contacts to prevent future delivery issues. If the email does not arrive after 5 minutes, click Resend Reset Link.

## Method 2: SSO-Authenticated Accounts

If your organisation uses SAML SSO (e.g., Okta, Azure AD, Google Workspace), your password is managed by your identity provider — not CloudDash.

To reset your password:
1. Contact your IT administrator or identity provider portal directly.
2. CloudDash does not store or manage passwords for SSO-enabled accounts.
3. Once reset at the IdP level, click **Login with SSO** on the CloudDash login page.

## Locked Out After Too Many Attempts

CloudDash locks accounts after 10 consecutive failed login attempts. The lockout period is 30 minutes. After 30 minutes, you may retry or use the password reset flow above. If you believe your account has been compromised, contact CloudDash Security at security@clouddash.io immediately.

## Changing Your Password (When Already Logged In)

1. Click your avatar in the top-right corner.
2. Select **Profile & Security**.
3. Under the **Password** section, click **Change Password**.
4. Enter your current password, then your new password twice.
5. Click **Save Changes**.
